intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Faulkner County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

limits: From the 2024 report, dated August 5, 2026. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Twin Groves
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer Schedule 1 shows a General Fund balance of $34,813, as of December 31, 2024. However, when the outstanding amount owed to the Street Fund for state aid totaling $46,529 is considered, the General Fund has a deficit balance of $11,716 for 2024. A similar finding was issued in the previous three reports.
